title: Leader Elements in an Array
statement:
An element of an array is called a **leader** if it is **strictly greater** than every element located to its right. The last element of the array has no elements to its right, so it is always a leader.

Given an array of `n` integers, print all of its leaders in the order in which they appear in the array (left to right).
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers.
output_format: Print the leaders as space-separated integers on one line, in left-to-right order.

examples.explanation: `1` is last, so it is a leader. `2 > 1` is a leader. The `7` at index 4 is greater than `2` and `1`, so it is a leader. The `3` is smaller than the `7` to its right, and the `7` at index 2 is only equal to the `7` on its right, so it is not strictly greater. `4` is smaller than `7`. Finally `9` beats everything to its right.
Only the last element is greater than everything to its right (it has nothing to its right).
Equal values do not count as strictly greater, so only the last `5` is a leader.

hints: Checking every element against everything to its right is O(n^2). Can you reuse information between positions?
Scan from right to left while remembering the largest value seen so far.
An element is a leader exactly when it is strictly larger than that running maximum. Remember the output must be in left-to-right order.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    best = None
    res = []
    for x in reversed(a):
        if best is None or x > best:
            res.append(x)
            best = x
    res.reverse()
    print(' '.join(map(str, res)))

main()

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
res = []
for i in range(n):
    ok = True
    for j in range(i + 1, n):
        if a[j] >= a[i]:
            ok = False
            break
    if ok:
        res.append(a[i])
print(' '.join(map(str, res)))
